items.headline: Circular-C reports progress; qualification remains unverified
items.what_changed: A July 6 project-partner disclosure reports lignin adhesive progress. June 10 dates the consortium meeting, not the underlying tests. Named standards and numerical results remain unavailable in this source. [S2]
items.why_it_matters: Editorial interpretation: this warrants technical follow-up, not an assumption of commercial readiness.
items.limitation: Exact wood-product classes, industrial trials and independent validation are not established by this announcement.
items.next: Request named standards, exact panel types, formulation and test reports; monitor larger-scale validation.
items.uncertainty: July disclosure date, not experimental milestone date. June 10 was a consortium meeting. Standards, test results and exact product qualifications remain unverified.

items.headline: BindEthics moves Ecohesive to 40 L production batches
items.what_changed: A July 10 company release says the brewing-waste adhesive has moved from laboratory testing to 40-litre production-grade batches, made with Chemique Adhesives, with initial batches earmarked for trials at European Tier 1 and eco-plywood manufacturers. [S4-bindethics-v1]
items.why_it_matters: Editorial interpretation: a contract manufacturer and named trial route make this worth a sample request. The 2,000 L figure is a stated pathway and the 6,000 t figure is customer interest; neither is production.
items.limitation: No recipe, solids, dosage, press cycle, panel test or independent qualification is published. "100% bio-based" and drop-in compatibility are supplier claims.
items.next: Request batch records, product type, press cycle, dosage and independent (Bangor or third-party) EN test reports from the announced Tier 1 trials.
items.uncertainty: Supplier-authored claims only: recipe, solids, dosage, press cycle, panel tests and independent qualification are absent. "Industrial-scale" describes 40 L batches; the 6,000 t figure is customer interest, not output.

items.headline: 5-HMF supply: ResiCare and Axens enter exclusive talks
items.what_changed: Michelin ResiCare announced exclusive negotiations with Axens on 8 July to license and deploy its 5-HMF technology, developed with IFPEN. A first unit of about 3,000 t/year at Péage-de-Roussillon is scheduled to start in early 2027. [S5-resicare-v1]
items.why_it_matters: Editorial interpretation: a dedicated 5-HMF supply would matter for aldehyde-type resins that avoid formaldehyde. The capacity is for a chemical intermediate, not adhesive.
items.limitation: Talks, not a concluded deal; plant not yet operating. No wood-panel formulation, emissions, cost or LCA data in this release.
items.next: Watch for a signed agreement, commissioning, 5-HMF specification and any third-party panel results for HMF-based resins.
items.uncertainty: Negotiations, not a concluded partnership. The plant is announced, not operating. No wood-adhesive formulation, emissions, cost or LCA data in the release.

items.headline: Residue lignins fully replace phenol in lab LF resins
items.what_changed: A July 8 PLOS One study made resol resins with lignin from chir-pine needles, eucalyptus sawdust or bagasse as the only phenolic component. Chir-pine lignin performed best (3.12 MPa dry lap shear) but stayed below the laboratory PF control (3.40 MPa). [S7-plos-lf-v1]
items.why_it_matters: Editorial interpretation: useful feedstock learning for phenolic substitution; it shows lignin structure, not total hydroxyl content, drives bond strength. Formaldehyde is still a reactant.
items.limitation: Three replicates, lap-shear joints only, laboratory rather than commercial PF benchmark; panel emissions not measured.
items.next: Seek panel-level tests (EN 314 / EN 319), free-formaldehyde and emission data, and a commercial PF comparison.
items.uncertainty: Three replicates per condition; laboratory PF rather than commercial benchmark; lap-shear joints, not panels; residual carbohydrates and panel formaldehyde emissions not measured.

items.headline: Acrylic-acid watch: enzyme cascade from methanol
items.organization: Tianjin Institute of Industrial Biotechnology, CAS
items.what_changed: A July 21 Nature Communications paper reports an engineered acrylic acid synthase in a cell-free methanol-to-acrylic-acid cascade, reaching 4.3 g/L in 16 hours in a 1 mL reaction. [S6-nature-maap-v1]
items.why_it_matters: Editorial interpretation: a route to acrylic monomers from one-carbon feedstock, relevant to the acrylic dispersion watch. It is upstream chemistry, not an adhesive result.
items.limitation: Methanol origin not stated, so renewable carbon is not shown. Cost figures are modelled scenarios. Formaldehyde is a pathway intermediate.
items.next: Look for isolated-product purity, enzyme productivity and reuse at larger volume, and a renewable-methanol chain of custody.
items.uncertainty: Millilitre-scale cell-free reaction; methanol origin of tested material not stated; product isolation, enzyme cost and scale-up are modelled or open. Formaldehyde is a pathway intermediate.
